card.title: IPhone Charging Circuit Diagnostics Guide

claims.statement: Expected input: PP_5V0_USB and PP_TRISTAR_PIN at 5 V on Tristar models; PP_VBUS1_E75 at 5 V on Hydra (up to iPhone 11) and Kraken (iPhone 12–14) models.
The charging IC doesn't validate the cable; the USB controller does. If it can't, cable charging fails but wireless still works, pointing at the USB controller/RVP path.
The 10 Ω resistor on PP_VAR_USB_RVP (iPhone 8/X and 13/14) should show ~5 V on both pads; one side only = open resistor or downstream fault.
PWR_GATE_EN_VBUS_1_VALID at 3.7–5 V (any voltage above 0) means the USB IC is working; 0 V means it's faulty or unpowered.
USB IC part numbers: NXP 1610A2 (iPhone 6/6 Plus), 1610A3 (6s/6s Plus/SE 1st gen), 1610A3B (7/7 Plus), 1612A1 (8/8 Plus/X/XR/XS/XS Max), 1614A1 (12 series), 1616A0 (13 series), 1618A0 (14 series).

procedure: Check 5 V at the cap before the charging IC.
If missing, check PP_VAR_USB_RVP and its 10 Ω resistor (5 V both sides).
Measure PWR_GATE_EN_VBUS_1_VALID (>0 V = USB IC OK).
If 5 V present but no charge, check charging IC output (~3.7 V) and CHG_BOOT cap.
card.caveats: The table's placement of iPhone 11 / SE 2020 is garbled on the source (listed under 1610A3B, but images group them with the 1612A1 models); verify by boardview. CHG_BOOT diode values on the source ('~9 V'/'~4 V') look like voltages and are not carried into readings. Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
